## Frequently asked questions  about Appspace Intelligence

What is workplace AI?

Workplace AI is artificial intelligence built into the tools people use every day at work, instead of being a separate chatbot bolted on top. It helps with communications, space booking, and content creation. In Appspace, that means AI that drafts copy, answers questions, and finds you a meeting room, right inside the platform you already have.

What is Appspace Intelligence, and how does it work?

Appspace Intelligence is the AI layer built into Appspace’s tools. It connects data across your Signage, Intranet, Workspace, and Visitors solutions. AI generates content, surfaces insights, and powers assistants that can take action (like booking a room or answering a question) right inside the tools your teams already use.

Do I need to buy or manage a separate AI tool?

Appspace Intelligence is built into the Appspace platform, not a standalone app to manage separately. It works inside Signage, Intranet, Workspace, and Visitors. You can also choose to connect the AI providers you already use to use their models in your workflows.

Which AI models does Appspace Intelligence support?

Appspace Intelligence runs on its own default AI model out of the box. You can connect providers like Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Foundry, or Gemini Enterprise, so you’re using the models your company already has agreements with.

Can I turn off AI features for specific teams or users?

Yes. You can enable or disable AI features by user or role, so you can roll features out to the teams that need them.

Does Appspace Intelligence support multiple languages?

Yes. Built-in translation lets content published in one language reach employees in the language they read best, without a separate translation tool or manual process.

Does Appspace Intelligence keep my data secure?

Yes. Appspace Intelligence runs on the same SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001-certified platform as the rest of Appspace, and IT can enable or disable AI features by user or role with granular governance controls. When you use your own AI model, AI requests route through the provider’s API, so you can track usage and cost on that account’s dashboards.
